fen_walk_spine.description: The only road on Fenris Isle runs from the pier to the manor, and Pier-Warden Hask has not set foot on it since the crossing. He has watched it from the jetty every dawn, and every dawn it looks a little narrower. He wants someone to walk it as far as the manor gate and tell him what has changed.
fen_walk_spine.accept_text: Village, crossroads, manor gate. Stay on the road. The isle does not like strays, and the ones who step off it tend to be found in the spring. If you meet anyone, do not ask their name. Ask where they are going.
fen_walk_spine.turn_in_text: The road holds. I thought it wouldn't. Thank you. I'll sleep on the pier tonight with an easy mind, which is a phrase I haven't used since the boat. Take this. It washed up last month and I never found the owner.

fen_shore_crawlers.description: The shore around the pier is crowded with tidewrack crawlers, picking at whatever the lake delivers, and rabid wolves follow them in for the scraps. Hask spends his nights listening to the clicking and the snarling. He wants a stretch of beach he can walk without a knife in his hand.
fen_shore_crawlers.accept_text: Anywhere along the shore. Crawlers dig in the shingle. Wolves wait at the edge of the tide. Eight crawlers, six wolves. Don't stand where the water is dark. Something has been leaving fish heads on the stones.
fen_shore_crawlers.turn_in_text: A shore a man can stand on. I'll hang a lantern and see who comes. Whoever it is, I'll be glad of the company, and gladder of the road they came by.

fen_cursed_shore.description: Elder Gravemoss guards what is left of Bloodmoon Village. The worgen stalkers creep closer every night, and the cursed villagers have started to look in the windows, patient as dogs at a butcher's door. The elder has lost count of the lamps he has lit. He asks that the ground around the village be cleared of both.
fen_cursed_shore.accept_text: Out in the open ground around the village. Stalkers hunt in threes and the villagers hunt in silence, so keep your back to the walls. Eight stalkers, six villagers. If one of them says your name, it only means they remember the shape of it.
fen_cursed_shore.turn_in_text: I can sleep, now, for a night or two. Thank you. It matters more than you'll know. I was a schoolteacher before the isle. The children I taught are the ones at the window, and I have not found the courage to teach them anything else.

fen_isle_banshees.description: The drowned still sing along the strand, and the banshees who sing back are the worst of it. They keep the whole isle awake with a long, high wail that comes in with the tide. Gravemoss has stopped trying to sleep and started trying to bargain. He would like the banshees quiet before he runs out of things to offer.
fen_isle_banshees.accept_text: The Cursed Shore, along the beaches. They sing at dusk, so be early. Eight of them. Don't listen to the words. They are not meant for you, and they are very persuasive.
fen_isle_banshees.turn_in_text: Quiet. I'd forgotten the quiet. It's almost worse. I keep listening for the song, and the silence listens back. Thank you, anyway. I'll find something to fill it.

fen_banshee_locks.description: Every banshee leaves a lock of hair behind when she fades, pale and wet, and it does not rot. Gravemoss has a theory that the locks are anchors, the last tether to whatever the women were. He wants five, to bury under the village stones where they might finally let go.
fen_banshee_locks.accept_text: From the banshees, after they fade. Gently. They remember being people, and I would rather you did too. Bring five. I'll dig the holes myself. It's the only part of this I can still do properly.
fen_banshee_locks.turn_in_text: They go in the ground by the well. It is the best I can do for them. I'll say a word over each, though I don't know their names. I think that is allowed.

fen_ancient_curse_beast.description: Something older than the curse walks the Cursed Shore: a bear the size of a barn, wrapped in its own rot. The villagers call it the Ancient Curse-Beast, and nobody who hunts it has gone twice. Gravemoss has recorded eleven attempts. He would like the twelfth to be the last.
fen_ancient_curse_beast.accept_text: It wanders the Shore. Follow the broken trees. The wolves won't go near it, which should tell you something. Kill four of them for the scent, and the beast will come. It is slow. Don't rely on that.
fen_ancient_curse_beast.turn_in_text: It was already old when the curse came. I'd like to think it's resting. Perhaps it only wanted to be left alone, as the rest of us do. Take your pick. It's the best we have.

fen_drowned_docks.description: The south-west docks are where the drowned come ashore, and the bilge rats come with them. Huntsman Corwell lost a boat there, and a nephew, and a good half of his temper. He wants the docks clear, so that someone, one day, might tie up a boat without wincing.
fen_drowned_docks.accept_text: The Drowned Docks, south-west of the village. Sailors on the beach, rats under the boards. Eight sailors, six swarms. Mind the planks. A fair few of them are not planks.
fen_drowned_docks.turn_in_text: A cleaner dock. I won't pretend my nephew's coming back. But the boat's safe to look at, and that is more than I had this morning. Thank you. I'll sit on it a while.

fen_harpoons.description: The Drowned Harpooners carry iron heads that Corwell's family forged, and every one of them is bent the same way, as though something very large took hold of them and pulled. He wants five for the smithy, to be melted down and made right, because he will not leave good iron to the lake.
fen_harpoons.accept_text: From the Drowned Harpooners at the docks. Take the heads, not the poles. The poles are rotten to the heart, and I won't have you hurt by a splinter.
fen_harpoons.turn_in_text: Bent by cold lake. I'll bring them back to something honest. A hook, maybe, or a plough. Something that spends its life being used. It is a better fate than most iron gets here.

fen_wretches.description: Waterlogged Wretches drag themselves up the beach at night. They were fishermen, once, and they still have the nets over their shoulders as though they might be called back to work. Corwell knows their faces. He would like to see them off the shore, and to know they are not coming back.
fen_wretches.accept_text: The beach at the Drowned Docks, and the shingle west of the jetty. Eight of them. If any wear a red scarf, make it quick. That one was my friend.
fen_wretches.turn_in_text: I knew four of them. I'm sorry for all of them. Thank you. I'll put their nets away. It's not much, but it's what I can do for a trade that fed this island.

fen_logbook_page.description: A page from a ship's log, pulled from a Drowned Sailor's pocket, stiff with salt. The last line reads: "The Captain locked the hatch from the outside." Huntsman Corwell kept the drowned ship's roster. He will know whose hand wrote it.
fen_logbook_page.accept_text: You read the line twice. Corwell, in the village, kept the roster. He will want to see this, and you suspect he will wish he never had.
fen_logbook_page.turn_in_text: So that is what happened to the Captain's crew. I'd wondered. I'd rather not have been right. Thank you. I'll add the page to the roster, and the name to the pile of things this isle has taught me not to forgive.

fen_captains_ghost.description: The ship's Captain still walks the docks, wrapped in water and rage, hunting the men he locked below. Corwell has the roster and the shame of it. He does not ask you to forgive the Captain. He asks only that it end.
fen_captains_ghost.accept_text: On the jetty at the Drowned Docks, at night. He looks for his crew. He will find you instead. Don't speak to him. He has heard every excuse, including his own.
fen_captains_ghost.turn_in_text: He'll trouble no more crews. I hope the lake gives him back his rest. Or doesn't. I am not sure which would be kinder, and I have stopped pretending I know.

fen_curs_grave.description: The east of the isle is a boneyard for hounds: worgs and curs bred for the Baron's hunt, buried with their masters in a long row of stones. Gravehunter Selke says they have started to dig themselves out, one by one, and she has not yet counted the holes.
fen_curs_grave.accept_text: The east lobe, past the crossroads. They dig around the old stones. Eight worgs, six curs. If you see a freshly turned hole, step around it. They're not always empty.
fen_curs_grave.turn_in_text: Fewer dogs underfoot. I'll take it. Selke thanks you, in her own gruff way, which is by not speaking for a long moment and then handing you something.

fen_collars.description: The Feral Packmasters wear the Baron's old collars: iron, studded, stamped with the Ashbury crest. Selke wants five, so that nobody, ever again, wears a collar with that crest. She has her reasons, and none of them are written down.
fen_collars.accept_text: The Packmasters in Cur's Grave. Cut the strap, don't touch the studs. They are sharper on the inside than the out. I would not bring one home to a child.
fen_collars.turn_in_text: A crest, five times over. The Baron owned everything on this isle, even the dogs. I'll melt them. A collar is a hard thing to put down, even when you're not the one wearing it.

fen_cur_wardens.description: The Cur-Wardens keep the graves and the dogs in them, and they speak in a language nobody has heard since the curse. Selke wants six of them quiet. She says she doesn't need to understand it to know it's a lullaby, and a bad one.
fen_cur_wardens.accept_text: Cur's Grave, among the stones. They chant at dusk. Six of them. If they begin to chant while you fight, stop and listen. It's the only thing that works.
fen_cur_wardens.turn_in_text: Quiet, at last. I don't need to understand what they said. I only need to know it stopped. Take your reward, and take it quickly. The dogs will notice the quiet, and they are not fond of it.

fen_alpha_cur.description: The hounds of Cur's Grave follow one: a scarred, grey, impossibly large cur, the Baron's last hunt-leader. Selke has watched him from the ridge for a month and has not once seen him sleep. She wants him off the boneyard.
fen_alpha_cur.accept_text: The middle of the boneyard, among the stones. You'll hear it first. He doesn't growl. He sighs, like something very tired. Do not take that for mercy.
fen_alpha_cur.turn_in_text: He led them well. I'll bury him with the rest. It's the least I can do. Whatever the Baron made him, he kept the pack together, and that is more than I can say for the Baron.

fen_manor_approach.description: Scout Merrin has watched Baron Ashbury's manor for three nights and has not seen a living thing. That does not comfort her. She wants someone to walk to the gate and into the forecourt, and come back with an honest report. She will not ask what the fountain looks like. She'd rather hear it from you.
fen_manor_approach.accept_text: The spine road north. Past the ridge walls, through the cracked gate, up to the fountain. Walk like you belong there. The ones who skulk are the ones who don't come back.
fen_manor_approach.turn_in_text: Nothing stopped you. That's what worries me. A house with a guard stops visitors. A house with no guard has already made its choice. Thank you for the report. I'll sleep on it, badly.

fen_manor_guards.description: Ashbury's guard never left their posts. Footmen walk the forecourt, guardians hold the gate, and none of them have been relieved in a century. Merrin finds it hard to hate them. She wants them relieved all the same, as a kindness, and as a necessity.
fen_manor_guards.accept_text: The manor forecourt and the walls either side of the gate. Six guardians, six footmen. Salute them first, if you can. They like to be addressed.
fen_manor_guards.turn_in_text: Relieved. The Baron will be lonely. Take your reward, and wash. The forecourt has a smell I will not describe, and it follows you home.

fen_manor_hounds.description: The Baron's hounds roam the manor grounds, and the worgen keepers feed them. Merrin has seen the keepers eat what they were meant to feed. She would like both kennels empty before somebody makes the mistake of knocking at the front door.
fen_manor_hounds.accept_text: The grounds around the manor, east and west of the forecourt. Six hounds, five keepers. Keepers first. Hounds are loyal. Keepers are only hungry.
fen_manor_hounds.turn_in_text: The grounds are quiet. The manor is not. I'd rather the quiet were the manor's, but I'll take what I can get. Well done. Your reward is by the gate.

fen_noble_signets.description: The Cursed Nobles of Fenris Proper still wear their house signets. Merrin wants four, to show the Rear Guard who sat at Ashbury's table when the curse was made. She believes someone, somewhere, will want to read those names aloud.
fen_noble_signets.accept_text: The Cursed Nobles in the forecourt and the manor grounds. Take the rings, not the fingers. Four of them. They'll look at you as though you were late to dinner.
fen_noble_signets.turn_in_text: Four houses, four names. The Rear Guard will want these. And perhaps the families. Some of them may still be alive, and may not know what their grandfathers dined on.

fen_baron_ashbury.description: Baron Ashbury ruled Fenris Isle alive, and rules it worse dead. He sits in the manor hall and waits for the next guest to disappoint him. Merrin would like to see him disappointed. She has not decided what he has done to deserve it, only that the list is long.
fen_baron_ashbury.accept_text: In the manor, past the forecourt. Dress for a funeral. His servants will present themselves before him. Let them. Then do what he cannot stop you doing.
fen_baron_ashbury.turn_in_text: The manor's quiet. The Baron is down. It's an odd thing to say, after all this. I'd expected to feel more. Mostly I feel tired. Take your reward. And don't look too long at the portraits.

fen_altar_arch.description: The curse was cast under the west ridge, in the Shadowpine Altar, and Warden Orlan has watched its arch for ten years. He wants someone to stand at the foot of the stair and tell him the air is still wrong. If it isn't, he may finally be allowed to go home.
fen_altar_arch.accept_text: The arch in the western ridge. The stair is below it. Stand at the bottom and breathe. Don't light a torch. If your breath fogs, it's still wrong.
fen_altar_arch.turn_in_text: Still wrong. Of course. Thank you for confirming. I'll put the kettle on. There's nothing else to do while the world doesn't mend.

fen_altar_cultists.description: The Shadowpine Circle never left: cultists and risen bone-warders keep the altar's rites going, long after the cause was lost. Orlan has heard them chanting through the stone every night for a decade. He wants them thinned, if not stopped.
fen_altar_cultists.accept_text: The Altar's passages and circles. Cultists cast, bonewalkers shield. Take the cultists first or the bonewalkers will outlast you. Eight cultists, six bonewalkers.
fen_altar_cultists.turn_in_text: The rites will go on, I suppose. But slower. Slower is something. Take your reward. And please, be careful of the stair going home. It is a long way up and a short way down.

fen_altar_aldric.description: Bonewarden Aldric keeps the Bone Circle, west of the stair, and has for centuries. He is made of the things he keeps. Orlan wants him unmade, so that the bones may be bones and the stair may be a stair.
fen_altar_aldric.accept_text: The Bone Circle, the western cavern. Walk the stair and turn left. He'll speak. He has a lovely voice. It doesn't make him any less a pile of bones.
fen_altar_aldric.turn_in_text: He was a good warden, once. He guarded the wrong thing. It's an easy mistake, and a common one, and I have made it myself. Thank you. I'll light a candle for him, if the stair allows it.

fen_altar_tael.description: Curse Keeper Tael tends the Moon Circle in the east, feeding the moonstone with whatever the cult throws at it. He doesn't need to be there. He has been there for centuries out of habit. Orlan is willing to say that is the saddest part.
fen_altar_tael.accept_text: The Moon Circle, east across the long road. Don't watch the moonstone. It watches back, and it's patient about it.
fen_altar_tael.turn_in_text: He won't tend it any more. The stone will dim, or it won't. Either way, thank you. I'll count the days. If it dims, I'll know. If it doesn't, I'll have an excuse to stay.

fen_altar_moonhowl.description: The Altar's worgen howl at a moon the cavern can't see. Orlan wants eight of them down, five of the wraiths that walk with them, and five moon-fangs for the cairn he is building at the arch. He says the cairn is a ward. He admits it is also a monument.
fen_altar_moonhowl.accept_text: The Altar's circles and the long roads between. Fangs from the worgen, not the wraiths. Eight worgen, five wraiths, five fangs. The wraiths do not carry anything, and they dislike being asked.
fen_altar_moonhowl.turn_in_text: A cairn of fangs. The curse should keep its distance for a season. Maybe longer. Take your reward. I'll set the last fang at dusk and see what the moon makes of it.

fen_altar_fenris.description: At the top of the Altar Ring, the curse has a shape: Alpha Fenris, the first worgen, the one the isle is named for. Orlan has waited ten years to see him dead. He has rehearsed what he would say. He has forgotten every word.
fen_altar_fenris.accept_text: The Altar Ring, at the top of the long climb. Take whichever road you prefer. They all end at his door. He is faster than he looks and he looks fast.
fen_altar_fenris.turn_in_text: Fenris is dead. After ten years, I'll sit, and stop watching the arch. I'd like to say I feel something. I think I'll feel it tomorrow. Take your reward. Come and drink with me, if you like. I'll even pour.

fen_isle_reckoning.description: Four reports have reached Gravemoss: the Curse-Beast, the Captain, the Alpha Cur and the Baron are all down. He would like the person who carried those four threads back to stand at the well, where he can thank them properly, in the old way, in front of anyone who cares to watch.
fen_isle_reckoning.accept_text: Back to the village square. Stand by the well. Don't hurry. The village will want to see you, and it's been a long time since it wanted to see anyone.
fen_isle_reckoning.turn_in_text: Four bosses, four reports, one hero. Bloodmoon Village has no gold to give you, so it gives you what it has. I hope it's enough. It's more than the isle has given anyone in a century.
